title: Word Search
description: Search a 2D grid for a word using DFS with in-place visited marking and backtracking.

data.text: Given an `m × n` grid of characters and a word, return whether the word exists in the grid. The word must be built from adjacent cells — horizontally or vertically — and the same cell may not be used twice.

**Input:** `board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]]`, `word = "ABCCED"`

**Output:** `true`

**Paths:** `A → B → C → C → E → D` moving right, right, down, down, left.

Try every cell as a possible starting point. From a cell, recurse into the four neighbours while the characters match. The 'no cell twice' rule is enforced by temporarily overwriting the visited cell with a sentinel, restoring it when the branch fails — that is the backtracking step and it avoids allocating a separate visited matrix.

data.title: DFS with in-place marking
data.content: Overwrite a visited cell with '#', then restore it.

data.title: Marking in place is safe because the grid is local state
data.text: The sentinel marks a cell as used *along the current path*. Once the branch is abandoned the sentinel is removed, so a later path can reuse the cell. This is exactly why a shared visited matrix does not work here — it would leak between paths.

data.title: Complexity and the cost of the first-character check
data.text: Worst case is O(m·n·4^L) for a word of length L, since each cell branches into up to four neighbours. Checking `board[r][c] != word[index]` before recursing is what keeps the branching factor low in practice.
Extension: Many Words in One Grid

Searching for a list of words one at a time repeats the same grid traversal. A trie of the target words lets all searches share a single walk of the grid — the subject of the 'Word Search II' variant. That is the reason the trie module is a prerequisite for this one.

data.title: Seeding the walk from a trie
data.content: The skeleton of Word Search II: one DFS, shared across all words.

data.caption: Every cell is a possible start; the DFS extends the path while characters match and undoes the visited mark on every retreat.

cards.title: In-place sentinel
pros: Undo is impossible to forget in the right place
cons: Mutates the input during the search

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: Grid DFS with backtracking is the pattern behind word search, connected regions, number of islands, and flood fill. The distinguishing detail is always the same question: what state must be restored when I retreat from a cell?
